central_unknown: The Madrid circuit (Madring) is brand new with zero F1 race history — only F3 testing and a Ferrari filming day exist as references. 19 red flags in F3 testing, unknown tire degradation, heavy curbs, dust on a green track, and a Monaco-like lack of overtaking opportunities make qualifying position and reliability the key unknowns.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: ML projects 27.5 exp pts, ppm 2.0, LOW risk, pred Q1→P2. All channels unanimously back Antonelli as the #1 captain — his record-breaking 93-point Monza weekend showed his ceiling, Mercedes is projected strongest constructor (68.3 exp pts), and the team had the best car recently. Even on a new track with limited overtaking, his qualifying pace should put him at the front. Wide 90% CI [-4.6, 49.0] reflects new-track volatility but the floor is manageable.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: George Russell
captains.reason: ML projects 25.1 exp pts, proj 37.5 pts (highest raw projection), pred Q2→P1 finish, but MEDIUM risk with 0.16 DNF probability. Russell is projected to win the race by the ML model and has the highest projected points ceiling. However, his wider CI [-11.3, 50.0] and higher DNF risk explain why Antonelli edges him on expected points. A differential captain pick if you believe Russell can convert a front-row start at a track where qualifying is king.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: At or near price floor, cannot lose value. Audi constructor exp 18.4 pts. Hulkenberg has been a consistent budget scorer — 14 pts at Monza — and channels highlight him as a safe budget fill enabling 4A builds. ML has Audi as decent value at 2.3 value score.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: Highly owned budget option on Racing Bulls. Still has price rise potential. Racing Bulls exp 25.8 constructor pts with LOW risk. Channels flag him as a core budget hold for 4A lineup structures.

buy.name: Lance Stroll
buy.note: At price floor, absolute minimum cost enables premium A-tier picks. Aston Martin may struggle on a power-hungry layout but cannot lose further value. Pure budget enabler.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: ML projects 10.2 exp pts, LOW risk, pred Q8→P8. A solid mid-budget option who has been rising in price. Stepping in at Red Bull and performing reasonably — channels see him as a budget-builder stopgap between B-tier and A-tier pricing.

consider.name: Fernando Alonso
consider.note: Recent price rise streak (24 pts at Dutch GP). Still has price rise potential, but Aston Martin likely struggles at power circuits. Multiple channels flagging him as a potential sell after Spain heading into Baku. High DNF history is a concern on an unforgiving new track. Consider holding if already owned but new buy is risky.

consider.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
consider.note: Audi's second driver, still has price rise upside. Channels note his qualifying can leave overtake points on the table. A budget alternative if Hulkenberg is already owned.

chips.name: 3x Boost
chips.reason: No grid penalties or obvious multiplier opportunities this weekend. The new track introduces massive variance — 19 red flags in F3 testing, Monaco-like difficulty, and unknown tire behavior. Channels who used 3x at Monza for Antonelli's grid penalty scored massive hauls (93 pts x3). Wait for a clearer asymmetric opportunity like a future grid penalty weekend (Russell penalty expected at Baku).

chips.name: 2x Boost (Captain)
chips.reason: Standard captain doubler — Antonelli is the consensus pick. ML projects 27.5 exp pts making him the clear 2x target with LOW risk.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: Budget building is the current meta priority. Channels suggest saving the wildcard for a future restructure, potentially around Baku when Williams gets their update and Russell takes his expected grid penalty. A wildcard then could enable maximum budget extraction.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: BoxBox analysis from Monza showed limitless scored lower than 3x boost. Save for a sprint weekend or a weekend with clearer pricing arbitrage opportunities.

watch_items: Friday FP1/FP2 will be critical — first time F1 cars run on this track. Track evolution, grip levels, and curb damage reports will reshape the running order. Delay final transfers if possible.
Ferrari filming day advantage: Ferrari and Pirelli ran a filming day at Madrid, giving Leclerc and Hamilton (plus the team) correlation data no other team has. Could give them a setup edge in FP1.
Tire degradation is a huge unknown — F3 testing showed significant tire issues on the new surface. High degradation could lead to more pit stops and strategy variance.
Turn 1 pile-up risk: Heavy braking zone into T1 compared to Singapore's disaster potential. Opening lap chaos could cause DNFs, especially in the midfield.

Track is compared to Saudi Arabia in layout character — high-speed, limited overtaking, qualifying position paramount. If this holds, captaining a strong qualifier like Antonelli/Russell is even more important.
George Russell grid penalty timing: Confirmed for Baku but some smoke about it possibly being moved. Monitor Mercedes communications closely before deadline.

Ferrari reliability concerns: Leclerc retired at Monza, and Ferrari's power unit has shown fragility at power-demanding circuits. Madrid's long straights could expose this again. ML gives Leclerc 0.14 DNF probability.
Weather: Early forecasts suggest possible rain on Friday (75%) clearing for Sunday. A wet FP1/FP2 would further reduce setup data on an already unknown circuit.
arc: Madrid is the first of a brutal power-circuit stretch: Spain → Baku → Malaysia (Sepang) → Cota → Mexico. Channels are warning that Ferrari's power unit will struggle across this run, making Mercedes and McLaren the premium constructors to own. George Russell's grid penalty is expected at Baku (Round 17), which could be the next big 3x boost opportunity. Williams' update arrives at Baku too, potentially unlocking Albon as a value play. The budget-building meta remains critical — channels emphasize accumulating value through B-tier price rises (Lindblad, Lawson, Hulkenberg) to fund 4A lineups. If Ferrari continues to underperform, selling Leclerc/Hamilton for a Mercedes double-up becomes the key strategic pivot over the next 2-3 races.
